Q: Unit testing - Find code coverage for conditions in mysql queries A:

You have answered your own question while asking "Query has to execute at leaset 3 times with different vakues [sic] of a_col to complete the coverage. How to ensure that coverage."

This is more of a unit test question than code coverage question. Any code coverage tool will consider the statement as being fully covered if the statement is called just once. Therefore your unit tests would need to account for each predicate evaluation that would need to be checked and so you will need to write at least three different tests, or, one test which includes a result set where a_col has all the required different values you wish to check for. Which is best is up to yourself.

Q: Failing to attach event listener to window object in nextjs A:

in 2026, React 19.2 (NextJs 16.2) has good enough useEffect to prevent repeated code running, so window.addEventListern("load", callbackFunction) is no longer needed.

I see when my NavBar component gets rendered many times, but its useEffect() runs only once. So you can run functions inside that useEffect(), then store data into a client state management. And use that to pass the data to the other components.

Q: Expo React Native: How to play notification sound for 30 seconds on Android? A:

I don't think expo-notifications is able to sufficiently cover your use case because IIRC it uses the NotificationCompat API, which has the following limitation:

Note: Beginning with Android 8.1 (API level 27), apps can't make a notification sound more than once per second. If your app posts multiple notifications in one second, they all appear as expected, but only the first notification per second makes a sound.

I'd rather look into using AlarmManager API for this. There is an expo package for it but I can't attest to it's quality. You might end up needing to write your own native bindings

Q: Am I missing any edge case or formatting requirement? A:

JOIN will exclude items which have no match, i.e., if a model has no revenue, then your query skips it. Also, kindly look at this experiment:

select '1985-07-27 00:00:00' between '1985-07-25' and '1985-07-27';
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| '1985-07-27 00:00:00' between '1985-07-25' and '1985-07-27' |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                           0 |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+

So the 27th of July 1985 is not between 25th of July and 27th of July, so if you want to include the last day of the year - which seems to be the case, then you need to use the next day as the second item of your between condition:

SELECT 
    c.name AS country_name,
    m.name AS motorcycle_model,
    SUM(s.quantity * m.price) AS revenue
FROM motorcycle_model m
LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.model_id = m.id
LEFT JOIN country c ON s.country_id = c.id
WHERE s.sales_date BETWEEN '2018-01-01' AND '2019-01-01'
GROUP BY c.name, m.name
ORDER BY c.name, m.name;

So I adjusted the right-hand-side of your between, made motorcycle_model as the point of departure and used LEFT JOIN instead of JOIN so if a motorcycle_model has no sales data in the period or it's missing a country in the database, then you'll still see it.
